note: Pitcairn Islands, read on 2026-10-30 on the Government of the Pitcairn Islands' immigration page (government.pn). A temporary worker must obtain a work visa before travelling (abroad), applying by email with medical, chest x-ray and police certificates and an application fee of NZ$300; the Governor decides after consulting the Island Council; work visas are issued for six months and may be extended before expiry (renewable). The page doesn't say whether the visa ties its holder to one employer, so that isn't written. To settle, one first lives on Pitcairn at least three months on a long-term visitor or work visa, then obtains a settlement visa (valid two years, NZ$500) by the family pathway (a spouse or partner, child, parent or sibling lawfully residing there) or the skills pathway (skills that will contribute to the community; written as a work route), and after lawfully residing more than two years applies for permanent residence (2 written), for which there is no fee; permanent residents may live and work on Pitcairn indefinitely (any work). Where the settlement visa is applied for isn't said in words. Decision times aren't stated; the seasonal resident and long-term visitor visas aren't written; naturalisation isn't on the page.

sources.title: Government of the Pitcairn Islands, Immigration
sources.said: If you wish to come to Pitcairn to work on a temporary basis, you will need to obtain a work visa before travelling. ... Pay the application fee (NZ$300) ... The Governor of Pitcairn will make decisions on applications for work visas, after consultation with the Pitcairn Island Council. ... Work visas are issued for six months. You can apply for an extension prior to expiry of the visa. ... Initially live on Pitcairn for at least three months on a long-term visitor visa or a work visa; ... Then obtain a settlement visa (valid for two years). ... the family pathway - where the applicant has a close family member – spouse/partner, child, parent or sibling, lawfully residing on Pitcairn; or ... the skills pathway - where the applicant has relevant skills which will contribute to the Pitcairn community; ... Then, after lawfully residing on Pitcairn for more than two years, apply for permanent residence. ... The application fee is NZ$500. ... There is no application fee for permanent residence. Permanent residents are entitled to live and work on Pitcairn indefinitely.
